questions.question: The mode of transmission of Ancylostoma duodenale : / a). Ingestion of eggs b). Skin penetration c). Mosquito bite d). Sexual transmission
questions.solution_html:
• The mode of transmission of Ancylostoma duodenale
  • (b) Skin penetration
  • Body is covered by a thick, flexible, and resistant cuticle that protects them from digestive enzymes
  • and host immune responses. The elongated, cylindrical, and tapering body helps them move easily
  • through host tissues. Hooks, suckers, or lips around the mouth for firm attachment to host tissues
  • (eg.Ancylostoma has cutting plates). Produce a large number of eggs to ensure survival of offspring.
  • Eggs and larval stages have thick protective shells to withstand unfavourable conditions. Show
  • reduction in sensory organs. Simplified digestive tracts suited to absorbing pre-digested host
  • nutrients. They can survive in oxygen-poor environments of the host intestine through anaerobic
  • metabolism.
  • (Any 3 points -(3Marks))
  • Complexity Simplest type of canal system More complex than asconoid
  • (5 marks))
  • Body Shape: The body of Polygordius is elongated, slender, and cylindrical, allowing easy
  • penetration through sand and mud.
  • Presence of Suckers and Hooks (Major Point): Powerful suckers (oral and ventral) help in firm
  • attachment to host tissues. Hooks on the scolex of Taenia solium assist in anchoring to the intestinal
  • wall. Fasciola hepatica has anterior and ventral suckers for clinging to bile ducts.

questions.question: Describe the organ system level of organization in animals.
questions.solution_html:
• Organ system level of organization means the body of an animal is made up of different organs that
  • work together to perform specific functions. Each organ is made of tissues. E.g.: digestive system
  • respiratory system etc. This type of organization is seen in more advanced multicellular animals
  • such as annelids, arthropods, molluscs, and vertebrates. It marks a high level of specialization and
  • division of labour among the organs and systems.
  • (Give full marks for relevant points)

questions.question: Define alloiogenesis and explain it with a suitable example.
questions.solution_html:
• Alloiogenesis in Platyhelminthes refers to the alternation of sexual and asexual generations in the
  • life cycle of certain parasitic flatworms. In the definitive host (usually a vertebrate), the adult worm
  • reproduces sexually, producing fertilized eggs that are released into the environment. In the
  • intermediate host (often a snail or invertebrate), the larval stages such as sporocyst and redia
  • multiply asexually, increasing the number of infective larvae.
  • Eg: In Schistosoma or Fasciola hepatica (liver fluke).
  • (Liberal valuation)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the locomotion, nutrition, and reproduction in Opalina.
questions.solution_html:
• Locomotion Opalina moves by coordinated beating of numerous cilia covering its body surface.
  • Cilia beat in a wave-like manner, producing smooth gliding movement. Movement helps it mix
  • with intestinal contents and maintain position in host. No specialized organ for attachment or
  • creeping. (1½ marks)
  • Nutrition: Holozoic and saprozoic mode of nutrition. Feeds on intestinal debris, bacteria, and
  • organic matter from host intestine. No cytostome (mouth); food is absorbed directly through the
  • body surface by diffusion or phagocytosis. Digestion is intracellular and nutrients are distributed
  • throughout cytoplasm. (1½ marks)
  • Reproduction: Asexual reproduction: By binary fission (transverse division) producing daughter
  • individuals. Sexual reproduction: By syngamy – gametes fuse to form zygote. Encystment occurs
questions.final_answer: individuals. Sexual reproduction: By syngamy – gametes fuse to form zygote. Encystment occurs

questions.question: Write short notes on the structure and functions of comb plates and colloblasts.
questions.solution_html:
•  Comb Plates (2½ marks)
  • Structure (1½ marks):Present in phylum Ctenophora . Formed of fused cilia
  • arranged in eight vertical rows called ctenes. Each row functions as a locomotory organ, forming a
  • comb-like plate.
  • Functions ((1 mark)): Locomotion – propel the animal smoothly through water. Maintain balance
  • and direction during movement. Help in spreading body currents for respiration.
  •  Colloblasts (2½ marks)
  • Structure (1½ marks): Unique adhesive cells found on tentacles of ctenophores. Each colloblast is
  • a straight filament, and a spiral filament. The sticky material helps in trapping prey. Nematocyst
  • absent.
  • Functions ((1 mark)): Used for capturing food by adhesion (not by stinging). Help in holding and
  • immobilizing prey before ingestion.
  • (Liberal valuation)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the significance of conjugation.
questions.solution_html:
• Conjugation is a type of sexual process seen in Paramecium, where two individuals temporarily unite
  • to exchange nuclear material. ((0.5 marks))
  • Rejuvenation: Conjugation restores vitality in organisms that have become weak due to repeated
  • asexual reproduction. It rejuvenates the cell by mixing nuclear material from two individuals
  • preventing degeneration. Nuclear Reorganization: Exchange and fusion of micronuclei lead to
  • reorganization of genetic material. This ensures normal nuclear function and maintains genetic
  • stability. Hereditary Variation: Conjugation introduces genetic variation by recombining genes from
  • two parent cells. Such variation helps in adaptation and evolution of the species. (Explanation of 3
  • points -(1.5 marks) each)
  • (NB: Please Give (2 mark) for explanation of conjugation and (1.5marks) for any 2 significance)
questions.final_answer: (NB: Please Give for explanation of conjugation and for any 2 significance)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the types of coelom and explain their significance in the classification of animals.
questions.solution_html:
• Coelom is the body cavity between the body wall and gut wall, lined by mesoderm. It provides
  • space for organ development and movement. Coelom is an important basis for classifying animals.
  • (Definition (0.5 mark))
  • Types of Coelom: 1)Acoelomate: No body cavity between body wall (ectoderm) and gut
  • (endoderm); space filled with mesenchyme. E.g.: Flatworms (Platyhelminthes). 2)
  • Pseudocoelomate: Body cavity present but not fully lined by mesoderm; derived from blastocoel.
  • E.g.:Roundworms (Ascaris, Nematoda). 3) Eucoelomate (True Coelomate): Body cavity fully
  • lined by mesoderm forming peritoneum; allows organ specialization.e.g.: Earthworm (Annelida)
  • Molluscs, Arthropods, Chordates.
  • (3 Types of Coelom with example labelled diagrame with explanation -(1.5 marks) each)
questions.final_answer: (3 Types of Coelom with example labelled diagrame with explanation - each)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

  • parts of India. Poor sanitation and unsafe water promote its spread. It affects mainly in children
  • and agricultural workers exposed to contaminated water. Associated with malnutrition and
  • anaemia in chronic cases.

questions.question: Describe the organ system level of organization in animals.
questions.solution_html:
• Organ system level of organization means the body of an animal is made up of different organs that
  • work together to perform specific functions. Each organ is made of tissues. E.g.: digestive system
  • respiratory system etc. This type of organization is seen in more advanced multicellular animals
  • such as annelids, arthropods, molluscs, and vertebrates. It marks a high level of specialization and
  • division of labour among the organs and systems.

questions.question: Define alloiogenesis and explain it with a suitable example.
questions.solution_html:
• Alloiogenesis in Platyhelminthes refers to the alternation of sexual and asexual generations in the
  • life cycle of certain parasitic flatworms. In the definitive host (usually a vertebrate), the adult worm
  • reproduces sexually, producing fertilized eggs that are released into the environment. In the
  • intermediate host (often a snail or invertebrate), the larval stages such as sporocyst and redia
  • multiply asexually, increasing the number of infective larvae.
  • Eg: In Schistosoma or Fasciola hepatica (liver fluke).
  • (Liberal valuation)

  • organisms that exist either singly or in colonies. Corals are divided mainly into hard corals (order

questions.question: Explain the locomotion, nutrition, and reproduction in Opalina.
questions.solution_html:
• Locomotion Opalina moves by coordinated beating of numerous cilia covering its body surface.
  • Cilia beat in a wave-like manner, producing smooth gliding movement. Movement helps it mix
  • with intestinal contents and maintain position in host. No specialized organ for attachment or
  • creeping. (1½ marks)
  • Nutrition: Holozoic and saprozoic mode of nutrition. Feeds on intestinal debris, bacteria, and
  • organic matter from host intestine. No cytostome (mouth); food is absorbed directly through the
  • body surface by diffusion or phagocytosis. Digestion is intracellular and nutrients are distributed
  • throughout cytoplasm. (1½ marks)
  • Reproduction: Asexual reproduction: By binary fission (transverse division) producing daughter
  • individuals. Sexual reproduction: By syngamy – gametes fuse to form zygote. Encystment occurs

questions.question: Write short notes on the structure and functions of comb plates and colloblasts.
questions.solution_html:
•  Comb Plates (2½ marks)
  • Structure (1½ marks):Present in phylum Ctenophora . Formed of fused cilia
  • arranged in eight vertical rows called ctenes. Each row functions as a locomotory organ, forming a
  • comb-like plate.
  • Functions ((1 mark)): Locomotion – propel the animal smoothly through water. Maintain balance
  • and direction during movement. Help in spreading body currents for respiration.
  •  Colloblasts (2½ marks)
  • Structure (1½ marks): Unique adhesive cells found on tentacles of ctenophores. Each colloblast is
  • a straight filament, and a spiral filament. The sticky material helps in trapping prey. Nematocyst
  • absent.
  • Functions ((1 mark)): Used for capturing food by adhesion (not by stinging). Help in holding and
  • immobilizing prey before ingestion.
  • (Liberal valuation)

questions.question: Explain the significance of conjugation.
questions.solution_html:
• Conjugation is a type of sexual process seen in Paramecium, where two individuals temporarily unite
  • to exchange nuclear material. ((0.5 marks))
  • Rejuvenation: Conjugation restores vitality in organisms that have become weak due to repeated
  • asexual reproduction. It rejuvenates the cell by mixing nuclear material from two individuals
  • preventing degeneration. Nuclear Reorganization: Exchange and fusion of micronuclei lead to
  • reorganization of genetic material. This ensures normal nuclear function and maintains genetic
  • stability. Hereditary Variation: Conjugation introduces genetic variation by recombining genes from
  • two parent cells. Such variation helps in adaptation and evolution of the species. (Explanation of 3
  • points -(1.5 marks) each)
  • (NB: Please Give (2 mark) for explanation of conjugation and (1.5marks) for any 2 significance)
questions.final_answer: (NB: Please Give for explanation of conjugation and for any 2 significance)

questions.question: Discuss the types of coelom and explain their significance in the classification of animals.
questions.solution_html:
• Coelom is the body cavity between the body wall and gut wall, lined by mesoderm. It provides
  • space for organ development and movement. Coelom is an important basis for classifying animals.
  • (Definition (0.5 mark))
  • Types of Coelom: 1)Acoelomate: No body cavity between body wall (ectoderm) and gut
  • (endoderm); space filled with mesenchyme. E.g.: Flatworms (Platyhelminthes). 2)
  • Pseudocoelomate: Body cavity present but not fully lined by mesoderm; derived from blastocoel.
  • E.g.:Roundworms (Ascaris, Nematoda). 3) Eucoelomate (True Coelomate): Body cavity fully
  • lined by mesoderm forming peritoneum; allows organ specialization.e.g.: Earthworm (Annelida)
  • Molluscs, Arthropods, Chordates.
  • (3 Types of Coelom with example labelled diagrame with explanation -(1.5 marks) each)
